stem: A streaming architecture has five downstream applications that each need a guaranteed, dedicated read throughput from the same Kinesis data stream, and separately needs a way to keep the S3 copies a Firehose stage delivers from turning into too many tiny files. Which TWO configuration choices address these two needs respectively? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Reducing the stream's retention period for the dedicated throughput need
Switching the stream to on-demand capacity mode for the dedicated throughput need
Registering each application as an enhanced fan-out consumer for the dedicated throughput need
Lowering the Firehose buffer size to its minimum for the tiny-file problem
Raising the Firehose buffer size and interval before delivery for the tiny-file problem

rationale: Registering each application as an enhanced fan-out consumer gives it its own dedicated 2 MiB-per-second read throughput per shard, independent of how many other consumers read the same stream. Raising Firehose's buffer size and interval accumulates more records into each delivered file before writing it to S3, producing fewer, larger files instead of many tiny ones. The stream's retention period only controls how long records stay available for replay, not per-consumer throughput. On-demand mode automatically scales the stream's total capacity but does not grant any one consumer a guaranteed dedicated share of it. Lowering the buffer size delivers smaller batches more often, which increases the number of small files rather than reducing it.
